title: A Population-to-individual Tuning Framework for Adapting Pretrained LM to On-device User Intent Prediction

problem.claim: User-intent prediction on smartphones is needed to support personalized assistants that anticipate activities from past interactions and context.

gap.claim: Existing research neglects diverse event sequences across dynamic contexts, and adapting pretrained language models for on-device intent prediction remains challenging.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes PITuning, a Population-to-Individual Tuning framework for adapting pretrained language models to on-device user-intent prediction.
PITuning uses dynamic event-to-intent transition modeling for common pattern extraction and adaptive unlearning strategies for long-tailed preferences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets report superior intent-prediction performance for PITuning.
The authors report that PITuning captures long-tailed preferences and is practical for on-device prediction scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Smartphones are positioned as platforms for personalized assistants that anticipate user needs.
Smartphone user-intent prediction is a pivotal step, but existing research does not adequately model diverse event sequences across dynamic contexts.
Although pretrained language models are promising, adapting them for on-device intent prediction is difficult.
PITuning addresses the challenge through population-to-individual tuning, transition modeling, and adaptive unlearning.
Experiments on real-world datasets report improved performance, long-tailed preference capture, and on-device practicality.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines common-pattern extraction with explicit handling of long-tailed preferences.

interpretation.claim: A user-intent system may need both population-level regularities and mechanisms for individual preference imbalance.

application.claim: When adapting pretrained models for personalized prediction, consider pairing transition modeling with adaptive treatment of infrequent preferences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination generalizes beyond the reported datasets or intent-prediction setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or hardware constraints.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details or computational and privacy trade-offs of PITuning.
